_what: Every machine (device) and every running inference engine (server) the workspace may call. Roles name MODELS (ROLES.json); this says where a model can be served. infer.py reads it on every call. Design: docs/ENGINES.md.
_adding_an_engine: An OpenAI-compatible engine (vLLM, SGLang, llama-server, LM Studio, and most new ones) is one entry with "engine": "openai" and no code. Anything else needs one adapter class in infer.py.

ollama-main._gpu: 2026-10-13 correction: this Ollama runs on the GPU. The 'skipping CUDA device ... cc=1210' line is its cuda_v12 library; cuda_v13 finds the GB10 right after it (library=CUDA compute=12.1) at almost every start. ONE start, 2026-10-12 00:52 local, came up library=cpu with ~25 GB free beside Swift -- GPU discovery failed under memory pressure -- and that process served the 7.1 tok/s bench. Restarted 15:44 local onto the GPU. A restart beside a full Swift can do this again: check `ollama ps` PROCESSOR after any restart.

swift._footprint: Measured 2026-10-06: the engine pid holds 84,531 MiB, and MemAvailable fell by ~95 GB with the FP8 PLE prewarmed into page cache.
swift._reasoning: Swift's chat template: reasoning_effort in xhigh|medium|low, default xhigh (the card's serving setting). think:true maps to xhigh.
swift._job_budget: -1 = until done (Jas, 2026-10-06: 'Whatever the model supports, why not just increase it to that maximum?'). vLLM stops at the end of the reply or when the 262,144 window fills; a larger max_tokens than fits is a 400 from vLLM, so 'no limit' is the maximum. Ollama's reason for a cap (one slot: a runaway blocked everything) does not hold on vLLM, where a runaway holds one of 4 slots. The backstop is the queue's wall clock (ask_q16 --timeout 5400).

vllm-swift.what: vLLM serving Swift 1.5 (serve.py, container `swift`). Its bridge IP is read from docker at call time (url_from); the url above is the last one seen.
vllm-swift._slots: The ENGINE CEILING = vLLM max_num_seqs 8 (serve.FLAGS seqs). It is no longer the lane count: since 2026-10-08 lanes belong to roles (Jas: 'add lanes for a role, not model'), set as Lanes on each role's Models-tab page, and modellease.slots = min(this, the sum of the lanes of the roles on this model). History: 4 -> 8 (2026-10-07), 8 -> 6 -> 1 (2026-10-08, after GPU-driver out-of-memory crashes); the 1 now lives on the Manager role as lanes: 1.
